items.answer: Augmented reality on the reality-virtuality continuum is the intermediate state in which the real environment is augmented with virtual content.

Virtual reality (VR) is, according to the Miriam Webster dictionary, an artificial environment experienced through sensory stimuli, in which sights and sounds play a primary role and are provided by a computer, possibly along with other sensory stimuli, and in which a person's actions partially determine what happens in the environment.

A virtual reality (VR) system is defined by three characteristics: an artificial or synthetic environment, sensory experience through computer-generated stimuli, and user actions that partially determine what happens in the environment; a system with these aspects can be categorized as a virtual reality system and distinguished from other systems, which are not supposed to have these aspects.
The six virtual reality (VR) content factors that affect cyber sickness (CS) are visual motion, means of locomotion, field of view, type of content, duration, and visual complexity.
Virtual reality (VR) hardware has three major components: displays (output devices), sensors (input devices), and computers (processing devices).

In the complete view of a virtual reality (VR) system, data flow from the organism to the VR hardware is labeled tracking, data flow from the VR hardware to the organism is labeled stimulation, and bidirectional data flows exist between the VR hardware and the surrounding physical world and between the surrounding physical world and the organism.
